The **52nd Annual Grammy Awards** took place on January 31, 2010, at [Staples Center](Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") honoring the best in music for the recording year beginning October 1, 2008 through September 30, 2009. [Neil Young](Neil_Young "Neil Young") was honored as the 2010 [MusiCares Person of the Year](MusiCares_Person_of_the_Year "MusiCares Person of the Year") on January 29, two days prior to the Grammy telecast. Nominations announced on December 2, 2009. The show was moved to January to avoid competing against the [2010 Winter Olympics](2010_Winter_Olympics "2010 Winter Olympics") in <Vancouver>. Only ten of the 109 awards were received during the broadcast.[[1]](52nd_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-1) The remaining awards were given during the un-televised portion of the ceremony which preceded the broadcast.

[Beyoncé](Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé"), who also received the most nominations, with ten, won a total of six awards breaking the record for most wins by a female artist in one night. [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") won four while [The Black Eyed Peas](The_Black_Eyed_Peas "The Black Eyed Peas"), <Jay-Z> and [Kings of Leon](Kings_of_Leon "Kings of Leon") won three. Artists who won two awards include [A. R. Rahman](A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman"), [Colbie Caillat](Colbie_Caillat "Colbie Caillat"), <Eminem>, [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West"), [Lady Gaga](Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga"), [Maxwell](Maxwell_(musician) "Maxwell (musician)"), [Jason Mraz](Jason_Mraz "Jason Mraz") and <Rihanna>. [Judas Priest](Judas_Priest "Judas Priest"), <AC/DC>, and [Imogen Heap](Imogen_Heap "Imogen Heap") each won a Grammy for the first time in their careers.

Taylor Swift's *[Fearless](Fearless_(Taylor_Swift_album) "Fearless (Taylor Swift album)")* was awarded the [Grammy Award for Album of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), at the time the youngest to win the award at age 20. "[Use Somebody](Use_Somebody "Use Somebody")" by rock band [Kings of Leon](Kings_of_Leon "Kings of Leon") won the [Grammy Award for Record of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), while "[Single Ladies](Single_Ladies_(Put_a_Ring_on_It) "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)")" by songwriters [Thaddis Harrell](Kuk_Harrell "Kuk Harrell"), Beyoncé Knowles, [Terius Nash](The-Dream "The-Dream") and [Christopher Stewart](Tricky_Stewart "Tricky Stewart"), was honored with [Grammy Award for Song of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"). [Zac Brown Band](Zac_Brown_Band "Zac Brown Band") was presented with the [Grammy Award for Best New Artist](Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), becoming the fourth country music act to ever win the award. They follow behind [LeAnn Rimes](LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes") in 1997, [Shelby Lynne](Shelby_Lynne "Shelby Lynne") in 2001 and [Carrie Underwood](Carrie_Underwood "Carrie Underwood") in 2007.[[2]](52nd_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2)

The **54th Annual Grammy Awards** were held on February 12, 2012, at the [Staples Center](Crypto.com_Arena "Crypto.com Arena") in [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") being broadcast on <CBS> honoring the best in music for the recording year beginning October 1, 2010 through September 30, 2011. [LL Cool J](LL_Cool_J "LL Cool J") hosted the show. It was the first time in seven years that the event had an official host.[[2]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2) Nominations were announced on November 30, 2011, on prime-time television as part of "The GRAMMY Nominations Concert Live! – Countdown to Music's Biggest Night", a one-hour special broadcast live on CBS from [Nokia Theatre](Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live "Nokia Theatre L.A. Live") at [L.A. Live](L.A._Live "L.A. Live").[[3]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-3)[[4]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-4) [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West") received the most nominations with seven. <Adele>, [Foo Fighters](Foo_Fighters "Foo Fighters"), and [Bruno Mars](Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars") each received six nominations. [Lil Wayne](Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), <Skrillex>, and <Radiohead> all earned five nominations. The nominations were criticised by many music journalists as [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West")'s *[My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy](My_Beautiful_Dark_Twisted_Fantasy "My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy")* missed out on a nomination for [Album of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") despite being highly critically acclaimed and topping many end of year charts.[[5]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-5)[[6]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-6) West's album went on to win [Best Rap Album](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album "Grammy Award for Best Rap Album").[[7]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-grammoff-7)

A total of 78 awards were presented following the Academy's decision to [restructure the Grammy Award categories](List_of_Grammy_Award_categories_from_2012 "List of Grammy Award categories from 2012"). [Paul McCartney](Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") received the [MusiCares Person of the Year](MusiCares_Person_of_the_Year "MusiCares Person of the Year") award on February 10, 2012, at the [Los Angeles Convention Center](Los_Angeles_Convention_Center "Los Angeles Convention Center"), two nights prior to the Grammy telecast.[[8]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-8)

On February 8, 2012, the Academy announced that the 54th Grammy Pre-Telecast Ceremony would stream live internationally. The ceremony took place at the Los Angeles Convention Center and was streamed live in its entirety internationally at Grammy's official website and CBS Television Network. The ceremony was co-hosted by [Dave Koz](Dave_Koz "Dave Koz") and [MC Lyte](MC_Lyte "MC Lyte"). A total of 68 awards were presented in the Pre-Telecast ceremony.[[9]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-PT-9) The official poster was designed by Architect [Frank Gehry](Frank_Gehry "Frank Gehry").[[10]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-10)

The day before the ceremony, [Whitney Houston](Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") died in Los Angeles, and the show's producers quickly planned a tribute in the form of [Jennifer Hudson](Jennifer_Hudson "Jennifer Hudson") singing Houston's "[I Will Always Love You](I_Will_Always_Love_You "I Will Always Love You")".[[11]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-11) The awards show began with a [Bruce Springsteen](Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") performance followed by an [LL Cool J](LL_Cool_J "LL Cool J") prayer for Whitney Houston. <Adele> won all of her six nominations, equalling the record for [most wins by a female artist in one night](Grammy_Award_records "Grammy Award records"), first held by [Beyoncé](Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé").[[7]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-grammoff-7)[[12]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-12) Adele became only the second artist in history, following [Christopher Cross](Christopher_Cross "Christopher Cross") in [1981](23rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "23rd Annual Grammy Awards"), to have won all four of the [general field](Big_Four_(Grammy_Awards) "Big Four (Grammy Awards)") ([Album of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), [Best New Artist](Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), [Record of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Song of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year")) awards throughout her career.[[13]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-13) [Foo Fighters](Foo_Fighters "Foo Fighters") and [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West") followed with five and four awards, respectively.[[7]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-grammoff-7)[[14]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-14) With his win for [Best Musical Theater Album](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Musical_Theater_Album "Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album") (for *[The Book of Mormon: Original Broadway Cast Recording](The_Book_of_Mormon%3A_Original_Broadway_Cast_Recording "The Book of Mormon: Original Broadway Cast Recording")*), producer [Scott Rudin](Scott_Rudin "Scott Rudin") became the 11th person to become an [EGOT](List_of_EGOT_winners "List of EGOT winners") winner.[[15]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-15)

## Ratings

The anticipation for the show's tributes to the late [Whitney Houston](Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") and the eventual record-tying wins by <Adele> greatly helped increased the ratings for the 54th Grammy Awards, which became the second highest in its history with 39.9 million viewers (trailing only behind the [1984 Grammys](26th_Grammy_Awards "26th Grammy Awards") with 51.67 million viewers). The rating was 50% higher than in [2011](53rd_Grammy_Awards "53rd Grammy Awards").[[16]](54th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-ratings-16) This remains the highest-rated Grammy telecast on 21st-century U.S. television.

The **55th Annual [Grammy Awards](Grammy_Award "Grammy Award")** were held on February 10, 2013, at the [Staples Center](Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") honoring the best in music for the recording year beginning October 1, 2011 through September 30, 2012. The show was broadcast on <CBS> at 8 p.m. ET/PT and was hosted for the second time by [LL Cool J](LL_Cool_J "LL Cool J"). The "Pre-Telecast Ceremony" was streamed live from LA's Nokia Theater at the official Grammy website. Nominations were announced on December 5, 2012, on prime-time television as part of "The GRAMMY Nominations Concert Live! – Countdown to Music's Biggest Night", a one-hour special co-hosted by LL Cool J & [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") and broadcast live on CBS from the [Bridgestone Arena](Bridgestone_Arena "Bridgestone Arena") in [Nashville, Tennessee](Nashville%2C_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee").[[2]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2) [Fun](Fun_(band) "Fun (band)"), [Frank Ocean](Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean"), [Mumford & Sons](Mumford_%26_Sons "Mumford & Sons"), <Jay-Z>, [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West") and [Dan Auerbach](Dan_Auerbach "Dan Auerbach") received the most nominations with six each.[[3]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-3)[[4]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-4)

<Gotye> and <Kimbra> won the [Record of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") for "[Somebody That I Used to Know](Somebody_That_I_Used_to_Know "Somebody That I Used to Know")", becoming the second Australian and first New Zealand act to win the award. [Mumford & Sons](Mumford_%26_Sons "Mumford & Sons") won the [Album of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for *[Babel](Babel_(Mumford_%26_Sons_album) "Babel (Mumford & Sons album)")*, and [Fun](Fun_(band) "Fun (band)") won the [Song of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") (with [Jeff Bhasker](Jeff_Bhasker "Jeff Bhasker")) for "[We Are Young](We_Are_Young "We Are Young")" as well as the [Best New Artist](Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist").[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) [Kelly Clarkson](Kelly_Clarkson "Kelly Clarkson") won the [Best Pop Vocal Album](Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album") for *[Stronger](Stronger_(Kelly_Clarkson_album) "Stronger (Kelly Clarkson album)")*, becoming the first and only artist to win the award twice.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) Dan Auerbach won the most awards during the ceremony, with five (including three as part of [The Black Keys](The_Black_Keys "The Black Keys")); followed by The Black Keys, Gotye, <Jay-Z>, <Skrillex>, [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West"), with three each.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) Other multiple winners include: [Chick Corea](Chick_Corea "Chick Corea"), Fun, Kimbra, Mumford & Sons, [Frank Ocean](Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean"), [Matt Redman](Matt_Redman "Matt Redman") and [Esperanza Spalding](Esperanza_Spalding "Esperanza Spalding") with two awards each.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5)[[6]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-6)[[7]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-7)

The Recording Academy introduced three new categories to the 78 awards previously presented at the [54th ceremony](2012_Grammy_Awards "2012 Grammy Awards")—[Best Classical Compendium](Best_Classical_Compendium "Best Classical Compendium"), [Best Latin Jazz Album](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Latin_Jazz_Album "Grammy Award for Best Latin Jazz Album"), and [Best Urban Contemporary Album](Best_Urban_Contemporary_Album "Best Urban Contemporary Album"), bringing it to a total of 81 awards.[[8]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-8) 70 of them were presented at the pre-telecast at the [Nokia Theatre](Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live "Nokia Theatre L.A. Live"), with the remaining 11 were presented at the main ceremony.[[9]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-Pre-telecast-9) [Bruce Springsteen](Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") received the [MusiCares Person of the Year](MusiCares_Person_of_the_Year "MusiCares Person of the Year") award on February 8, 2013, at the 23rd Grammy Benefit Gala at the [Los Angeles Convention Center](Los_Angeles_Convention_Center "Los Angeles Convention Center"), two nights prior to the main ceremony.[[10]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-MusiCares-10) The official poster was designed by Artist Erika Iris Simmons.[[11]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-11) The program producer is AEG Ehrlich Ventures, with Ken Ehrlich serving as executive producer, Louis J. Horvitz as director and David Wild and Ken Ehrlich as writers.[[12]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-JT-12)

The **57th Annual Grammy Awards** were held on February 8, 2015, at the [Staples Center](Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), <California>. The show was broadcast live by <CBS> at 5:00 p.m. [PST](Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") ([UTC−8](UTC%E2%88%9208%3A00 "UTC−08:00")). Rapper [LL Cool J](LL_Cool_J "LL Cool J") hosted the show for the fourth consecutive time.[[2]](57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2)

The Grammy nominations were open for recordings released between October 1, 2013, and September 30, 2014. Breaking from tradition of a prime-time concert approach, the Grammy nominees were announced during an all-day event on December 5, 2014, starting with initial announcements on the *[CBS This Morning](CBS_This_Morning "CBS This Morning")* telecast, followed by updates made through The Grammys' official <Twitter> account.[[3]](57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-3)
